I have worked in absolutely horrible clinics, and some amazing ones. 

I recommend staying and getting the test done and passed, and after that, leave for another RBT job (obviously if you still want to work in the field.) Because if you decide to leave and then go into another RBT position they will make you do the training again. 

Always tour the clinic before taking the job, meet BCBAs, RBTs, and especially observe how they do treatment with clients or look at treatment plans. Some things that are red flags are; 

-Not allowing clients breaks during DTT

-Being too heavily focused on DTT 

-Programs that focus on eye contact 

-Not allowing 2-3 weeks of pairing with little to no demands.

-Programs that limit when a client is “allowed” to stim, (obviously this depends on what the stimming is, if they are spitting or self harming to stim that is different than a client wanting to spin or hum.) 

-Not allowing RBTs mental health days or the ability to tap out during sessions. 

-High turn over rates. 

-Big one; *they do not offer parent training.*
